Today we will discuss the organization Jamaata Islami Hind or JIH. To understand this reality, let's look at how JIH describes itself. If you visit their website, you will read many things that sound positive and benign. They describe themselves as a social religious organization that stands for justice and equality. They even claim to be active in the promotion of democracy and human rights. But we must ask what do these words really mean? This is where we see the gravity of an ideology that hides in plain English. Analysts point out that if you translate the core concepts from this sanitized language, they sound exactly like the ideology preached by outfits like the Muslim Brotherhood which is a banned terror organization in many countries. The true objective is stated clearly if you know how to read it. Kamatin. This is defined as establishing and upholding the Islamic way of life. And they are clear this applies not just to individuals but to reforming all collective institutions. This is not a call for personal faith or religious freedom. It is a political blueprint to reconstruct our society. It is a form of Islamic politics that engages with the world with a single unchangeable mandate to solve every problem with the only tool it has its specific interpretation of Islam and to make that the guiding principle for the entire nation replacing our secular framework. To understand the root of this ideology, we must understand its founder Abula Mudi. He was one of the most influential Islamist thinkers [music] of the 20th century. Maudi's ideology is built on a core concept [music] he called hakimeia which means the absolute sovereignity of God alone which is Allah. From this he argued that any system based on popular sovereignity like secularism, democracy or nationalism is fundamentally illegitimate. For Mudi, the goal was not to coexist within a pluralistic democratic framework, but to replace it with an Islamic state or a kilafat governed exclusively by Sharia law. Jamat Islami was established in 1941 to achieve this very objective. After partition it was split and Jamati Islami Hindu was formed in India. While its public poster has evolved, critics argue that this core ideology of Maudi remains [music] its guiding principle. Maudi's ideas did not exist in a vacuum. They found a powerful parallel in the ideology of the Muslim Brotherhood found in Egypt by [music] Hassan Ala. Both the movements shared the same ultimate goal. [music] The establishment of an Islamic state and the rejection of secular governance. In the West, intelligence agencies have been concerned for decades about the Muslim Brotherhood's strategy. A key piece of evidence often cited is a 1991 document from a meeting of their members in the United States. The document known as the explanatory memorandum outlines a strategy of what it calls civilization jihad. This is not about violence in the conventional [music] sense, but about a long-term gradual process of infiltrating and weakening western societies from within using the very freedoms those societies provide. Concerns are now being raised that a similar blueprint is being followed in India. The now banned popular front of India or PFI had a document titled India vision 2047 which security agencies alleged was a road map to subjugate Hindus and establish Islamic rule by the 100th anniversary of India's independence. This points to a shared long-term strategic vision among such groups. So how did this strategy manifest in India? Analysts point to a multi-pronged approach. First, there is the public facing activity, a form of takia or strategic dissimilation. JIH runs schools and charities and presents itself as a moderate mainstream organization. A classic example of this strategic shift is its evolving stance on democracy. While Maudi's core philosophy rejects secular democracy, the organization now actively participates in elections. This isn't a change of heart. It's a change of tactics. It mirrors the Muslim Brotherhood's own declaration that democracy jihad is the new way, a patient strategy to use the tools of democracy to one day dismantle it from within. Second, there's a strategy of intellectual and political infiltration. They actively engage with secular intellectuals, media personalities and activists. They position themselves as a champion of civil liberties. This allows them to fool the seculars using the language of the Indian constitution to methodically hollow out its spirit. The left and liberal ecosystem in their opposition to the current government often fail to recognize the long-term agenda, inadvertently becoming what some analysts call useful idiots. Third, they exploit existing social fault lines. They actively work to co-opt and weaponize identity politics, framing every issue through the lens of oppression. They seek to build alliances with agrieved groups including SC's SD and OBC communities by presenting the Indian state and Hindu society as a common enemy. In fact, the now banned PFI was audacious enough to state this strategy in its internal documents. They explicitly mentioned using concepts like Ambedkar, the national [music] flag and our constitution as tools. a camouflage to shield their real intention of establishing Islamic rule while reaching out to these very communities.
